title: The Nihilist Reading Of The Phantom of the Opera (novel) #Shorts
description:
The self that experiences The Phantom of the Opera (novel) is a committee, not a king. It was first published as a serial in Le Gaulois from 23 September 1909 to 8 January 1910, and was released in volume form in late March 1910 by Pierre Lafitte. The novel is partly inspired by historical events at the Paris Opera during the nineteenth century, and by an apocryphal tale concerning the use of a former ballet pupil's skeleton in an 1841 production of Carl Maria von Weber's Der Freischütz.

The cold light on The Phantom of the Opera (novel) leaves the facts intact and only the comfort removed. There have been many literary and other dramatic works based on Leroux's novel, ranging from stage musicals to films to children's books. Some well-known stage and screen adaptations of the novel are the 1925 film and the Andrew Lloyd Webber musical.
